failure_modes.cause: Low Reynolds number (Re=19) and heterogeneous catalyst packing may lead to uneven flow distribution, reducing effective contact time and conversion below target (X=0.37)
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement structured catalyst packing or monolith; validate with tracer studies to ensure uniform residence time distribution

failure_modes.cause: At low Q (0.24 mL/min) and Re=19, gas (H2) and liquid (MeOH) may separate due to gravity or poor mixing, leading to inconsistent stoichiometry and potential dry spots on catalyst
failure_modes.mitigation: Use static mixers or segmented flow generators upstream of catalyst; monitor pressure drop fluctuations as proxy for phase behavior

failure_modes.cause: Back-pressure regulator (BPR) set at 5.0 bar may drift or fail open, causing pressure drop below methanol vapor pressure (0.84 bar) at 60°C, leading to solvent flashing and potential H2 release
failure_modes.mitigation: Install redundant pressure monitoring with automatic shutdown; use high-precision BPR with regular calibration checks

single_points_of_failure: BPR valve — failure causes pressure loss and potential solvent flashing
Catalyst bed — blockage or channeling stops reaction efficiency
H2 supply line — leak or interruption halts reaction and creates explosion hazard
validation_experiments: Run tracer study (e.g., dye or salt) at Q=0.24 mL/min to measure residence time distribution and detect channeling
Monitor pressure drop across catalyst bed over 24 hours at 60°C and 5.0 bar to detect fouling or channeling onset
Simulate BPR failure by manually reducing pressure to 1.0 bar and verify automatic shutdown system activates within 5 seconds
